the highest concentrations of metals and metalloids were found in the liver and the lowest concentrations in muscle; the highest genotoxic effects were observed in gills; the highest genotoxity was found in Pestan and the lowest in Zlatar.

the levels of metals and metalloids in water, sediment, liver, gills and muscle of the European chubs from three water bodies in Vojvodina, Serbia were below the threshold values for fish and human health.
the levels of metals in the examined sites are not high enough to induce genotoxicity, but that other xenobiotic compounds, possibly organic, contribute to the observed genotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the sources and routes of metal pollution in water bodies and the impact on aquatic biota.
the determination and comparison of metal and metalloid content in the sediment and water, and the determination of the genotoxicity of the water, expressed through DNA damage in fish tissues.

the assessment of the status of the water bodies, which are important for Serbia, but are also important for the whole of Europe, as they are situated on the Danube river, which is one of the largest and the longest rivers in Europe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the levels of metals in water bodies in Serbia are low, which is not reflected in the genotoxicity of the water.
the levels of metals in tissues of European chubs from examined sites are not alarming, but that the levels of genotoxicity are.

the results of our study do not support the hypothesis that metal and metalloid contamination of water and sediments is the major factor in genotoxic damage in European chub in the examined water bodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the European chub from the Zlatar Reservoir is the most exposed to genotoxicity and the least exposed to metals and metalloids, while the European chub of the Pestan River is the most exposed and the least genotoxic.
the results obtained in this work show that there is no clear link between metal and metalloid contamination and genotoxicity.
the level of DNA damage was not related to metal and metalloid content in tissues and water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tissue selection is important in environmental monitoring studies and that genotoxicity assays are useful tools to complement chemical analyses.
tissue selection is a crucial factor for monitoring studies and that genotoxicity should be used as an additional tool to assess the impact of pollution on aquatic organisms.
the comet assay can be a useful biomarker in the assessment of environmental genotoxicity.
